Comment: "Indefinite NPs which are nonspecific may also be marked with taha (indefinite pronoun). Nonspecific absolutive NPs may or may not bear the absolutive marker e."(Seiter 1979: 40)
“Niuean … is a strict VSO language with an ergative system of case marking.” (Seiter 1979: 1)
Inanimate pronouns are absent, but when inanimate full NPs occur, they follow the same ergative-absolutive pattern.
Absolutive marking can drop before au or with nonspecific NPs.
he marks both ergative and possessive; distinction via context.
Instruments and comitatives use aki e and mo e (absolutive), not ergative he.
